record.short: Warp Factories plans change from Pay as you go $0, Build $20 and Business $50 per user to Start $0 + usage and Scale $250 per team per month, with a new $3.50 per agent hour platform fee.
record.headline: Warp Factories replaced its Pay as you go, Build and Business plans with Start and Scale plans, priced per team plus usage, and added a platform fee billed in agent hours.
record.who: Teams building on Warp Factories; the Warp terminal plans (Free, Build, Max, Business) are unchanged.
record.read: Factories moves from per-seat tiers to per-team pricing with a metered agent hour fee on top of inference and compute, so cost now tracks runtime rather than seats. The Factories section also moved to the top of the page, which suggests it is becoming a main product.
record.caveat: Terminal plan prices ($20, $200, $50 per user) read the same before and after; only the Factories section was restructured. No company statement was found.

record.short: Zoho One adds a permanent free plan for up to 3 users with free editions of 16 apps, available only in LATAM (excluding Brazil).
record.headline: Zoho One now offers a Free plan with no time limit and no credit card, giving small teams free editions of 16 Zoho apps for up to 3 users.
record.who: New and lapsed Zoho One customers in LATAM (excluding Brazil); it can also be used after a trial or a cancelled subscription.
record.read: A free landing tier that sits behind the 30-day trial gives small teams a permanent entry point and an upgrade path to the paid plans. The regional limit suggests a test in one market before wider rollout.
record.caveat: Page says the plan is currently available only in LATAM (excluding Brazil); add-ons and classic support are not included.
